result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers are strong and nearly identical in structure: both put Item first, right-align quantity with tabular figures, use one en-GB date format, place a category chip filter above the table and keep the header sticky. A edges ahead because its header has its own background with uppercase muted labels, and its filter has a visible 'Category' label, which ties it more clearly to the table. B's header uses the same background as the rows and is set apart only by a heavier bottom border, though B adds tabular figures on dates and handles items with no expiry date neatly. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both put Item first, right-align quantities with tabular figures, use one date format (en-GB '5 Oct 2026'), and place category chips with counts above a scrolling table with a sticky header. B's header is easier to tell apart: it has a tinted background and uppercase labels, and it uses border-collapse: separate, so the line under the sticky header stays put while scrolling. A's white header with border-collapse: collapse can lose that line. B also labels the filter row 'Category' and puts the live count right above the table, while A puts it in a footer. B's fixed reference date keeps the demo expiry flags meaningful, but A's flags will drift toward 'Expired' over time.
